text:
alice: Customer ACME is seeing a return of 429s on our Dedicated pool after we bumped their quota yesterday. They increased from 300/min -> 1800/min and still getting rejections.
ben: Can you paste an example request/response? Is this exclusively from the dedicated pool or hitting hosted fallbacks?
alice: Dedicated only, pool id `dedicated-us-west-2-07`. Sample response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` body: `{\"code\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"message\":\"tenant rate exceeded\"}`. Happening around bursts, not constant.
carla: :eyes: any recent deploys to the rate-limiter or autoscaler last 24h?
dmitri: We rolled a small autoscale fix 3h before the first report. Not touching quota code. However there was a config change to the quota conversion util last week.
alice: I ran quick repro loop from their load generator:

```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}' -o /tmp/r$i.json &
done
wait
grep -c '429' /tmp/r*.json
```

Got 27 429s in a 200 call burst.
ben: That suggests token bucket refill mismatch under burst. Did the quota update propagate to the rate limiter instances? admin API returned 200 but may be a unit mismatch.
carla: I pulled the tenant quota record from the DB (sanitized):

```
{ tenant: "acme", rate_value: 1800, rate_unit: "minute" }
```

Our rate limiter expected `rate_unit: "per_min"` historically; the new conversion code accepts freeform and converts but I see a bug where `"minute"` was treated as seconds in some code paths.
dmitri: If the limiter treated 1800/min as 1800/sec it should allow more, not less. Another possibility: burst window uses a separate denominator. Check dataset: `burst_tokens = floor(rate_value * burst_multiplier / window_seconds)` - if window_seconds was accidentally set to 60*60 somewhere (3600) instead of 60 it would massively reduce tokens.
carla: Found it. In the dedicated pool path we accidentally used `window_seconds = config.rate_window_seconds || plan.window_seconds` and for dedicated the plan is missing `window_seconds` and fallback default got set to 3600 in a previous PR. So 1800/min became 1800/3600s -> 0.5 r/s effectively, with a burst cap rounding down in the limiter to 0 for small bursts -> immediate 429s.
alice: Nice find. That explains why increasing quota looked like no-op for bursts.
ben: Repro steps for infra: 1) ensure tenant is in dedicated pool, 2) set tenant quota to 1800/min via admin, 3) run the curl loop above, 4) observe ~10-30 429s in a 200-burst.
carla: Quick patch: set default `window_seconds` for dedicated to 60 and add validation to admin API: reject quota records with ambiguous `rate_unit` or missing `window_seconds` for dedicated plans. I'll open a PR.
dmitri: Operational mitigation: we can hotfix by forcing `window_seconds=60` for acme via admin override and flush limiter state. How to flush: call limiter admin endpoint `/admin/flush-tenant-cache?tenant=acme` and then toggle plan to re-trigger token refill.
alice: I tested admin override and flush on staging: after override + flush, burst run returns 0 429s on the same script.
carla: ETA for prod patch? I can do a quick hotpatch to defaults and validation, create rollout to dedicated-ratelimiter group. Will coordinate with SRE for a 10m window.
ben: I'll prepare rollback and watch dashboards: `dedicated.pool.us-west-2-07.429_rate` and `tenant.acme.429_rate` and latency SLOs. Pager on if >50 429s in 5m.
alice: Customer notified: "We found a config window mismatch; engineering is applying a safe hotfix and will follow up with an RCA." They acknowledged and asked for ETA.
carla: PR opened: #4927, patch sets default window_seconds=60 for dedicated and adds admin validation. Also adds a migration script to patch tenants that lack window_seconds.
dmitri: After patch we should run a short rollout and force a token refill for all tenants in the pool to avoid residual underfilled buckets.
alice: Action items: [carla: hotpatch + PR], [dmitri: prepare flush script + monitor], [ben: monitor + rollback plan], [alice: customer comms].
quota-bot: Automated note: quota record change detected for tenant acme at 3102467950 by alice.
alice: thanks team, updating customer; will reconvene if spikes reappear. :thumbsup:
